system_description.narrative_title: A Fracturing, Resource-Driven Global Order in Flux
system_description.narrative_summary: The system is an intertwined, open geopolitical-economic process driven by simultaneous regional wars (Ukraine, Iran–Gulf tensions, Israel), competing great‑power strategies (US, China, Russia, EU), and cascading stress across energy, finance and supply chains. Central banks, soaring oil profits, and political crises in major democracies amplify instability, producing volatile markets, fractured multilateral institutions, and frequent localized shocks that propagate globally. Policy responses and corporate adaptations (refining booms, strategic storage, military deployments, migration controls) are continually reshaping flows of capital, fuel, and influence.
system_description.scope: Nation-states and coalitions; regional conflicts and military postures (Middle East, Ukraine, Indo‑Pacific); global energy and commodity flows and firms; international financial system and central banks; multilateral institutions (UN, G20, EU); markets (oil, bonds, equities); supply chains, migration and humanitarian flows; political movements and domestic governance crises
system_description.super_system: Planetary socio‑economic and ecological system (global civilization interacting with planetary limits, climate change, and transnational risks)
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy & commodity markets (production, refining, shipping, strategic reserves)
International financial and monetary system (central banks, credit, sovereign debt markets)
Regional security architectures (Middle East, Europe, Indo‑Pacific security frameworks)
Global trade & supply chains (manufacturing, tech access, logistics, sanctions)

variables.name: Gulf maritime escalation
variables.description: Iran and regional Gulf actors are escalating maritime attacks on commercial shipping and naval postures, raising the prospect of wider military spillovers and diplomatic mediation.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war dynamics
variables.description: Russia’s large‑scale offensive and Ukraine’s sustained resistance are continually shifting battlefield control, striking logistics and energy infrastructure, and driving international military, economic and humanitarian responses.

variables.name: China strategic tech and maritime push
variables.description: China is tightening domestic political control while expanding state‑led efforts in advanced semiconductors and maritime patrols, changing access to critical technologies and regional security balances.

variables.name: Global oil market reconfiguration
variables.description: OPEC+ production choices together with major refiners and storage investments are reallocating supply resilience and profit centers, generating price volatility and shifting leverage in energy markets.

variables.name: European political and monetary strain
variables.description: European Union and eurozone institutions face mounting political fragmentation, slowing growth, debt stresses and a contested central‑bank succession that are straining cohesion and collective policymaking.
